messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT: tenant=acme-prod p99 request latency spike detected (baseline ~420ms -> 3.8s) for /v1/generate. 5m window.
Maria G: raising here — customer reported degraded responses and errors, escalated at 10:12. they see timeouts and a lot of queued requests. attaching snippet from their timeline.
Maria G: repro note from customer: intermittent 503s and sustained long tails. says spike correlates with heavy batch jobs at 09:58.
Samir K: looking. do we have per-tenant concurrency/backpressure metrics? I can check admission reject rate and active workers.
Alex T: I pulled the dashboard — admission rejects for acme-prod jumped from 1% -> 27% coincident with CPU saturation on worker-pool-5 and high KV cache thrash. p95 ~1.2s, p99 ~3.8s.
Erin P: sounds like worker saturation + expensive prompts. any change in model variant or payload size?
Maria G: customer says model=redwood-compat-13b, average seq len ~900 tokens for the batch jobs, before spike typical was ~120.
Alex T: that explains KV cache pressure. big sequence lengths kill throughput. I'm going to try a quick mitigation: warm up a standby pool and shift traffic, and temporarily reduce concurrency for large-seq requests.
Alex T: runbook steps I'm doing:
```
# promote standby pool for acme-prod
kubectl label nodes nodepool-standby redwood-tenants=acme-prod --overwrite
# admission change (temporary): reduce per-connection concurrency for long seq
redwoodctl admissions update --tenant acme-prod --max-inflight 8 --long-seq-threshold 512
```
Maria G: noted. i'll tell customer we're doing a temporary routing + admission tweak and ask for a time window for the big batches.
Samir K: can you also add a short-term fallback policy so requests that exceed latency SLO are routed to a smaller model variant? reduces cost and keeps success rate up.
Alex T: yep — adding a fallback rule to route >1s tail to redwood-7b-quant until we stabilize. doing canary now.
Erin P: also recommend enabling prefix/KV cache retention bump for acme-prod for 30m to reduce re-compute on repeated long sequences. I'll open a ticket to check kernel selection logs to see if quantized kernels regressed.
Maria G: customer update: they paused their scheduled batch job for 20m while we stabilize. will monitor.
Samir K: results so far: after admission throttles and fallback the p99 dropped to ~1.1s in the last 5m and rejects down to 6%. still above baseline but acceptable for now.
Alex T: leaving the canary for 15 more minutes, then we'll either roll forward or rollback. the longer-term ask: add auto-detect for long-seq bulk jobs to place them on dedicated warm pools instead of shared.
Erin P: Agreed — raising infra improvement ticket (INFRA-841) for long-seq routing + admission heuristics and a perf regression check for quant kernels.
Maria G: next actions for support: 1) confirm customer pause window and ask them to reschedule big batches to off-peak, 2) monitor p95/p99 in support dashboard, 3) follow up with eng for permanent fix.
Samir K: i'll own incident follow-up and patch proposal. tagging for handoff: @Alex T and @Erin P for runtime/root-cause.
Maria G: thanks team — I'll keep customer posted and close the loop once we confirm stability. :thumbsup:
